lessons.title: Theory of equations and reciprocal equations
lessons.summary: Reciprocal equations have coefficients symmetric from the leading term to the constant term. Their nonzero roots occur in reciprocal pairs because replacing x by 1/x reverses the polynomial.

lessons.title: Translation and rotation of coordinate axes
lessons.summary: Changing coordinate axes changes the numerical description of a fixed point. Translation changes the origin; an orthonormal rotation changes the directions without changing lengths or angles.

lessons.title: Pair of straight lines and homogenisation
lessons.summary: A homogeneous quadratic in two variables can represent two lines through the origin. Factoring its quadratic form reveals the directions and whether the lines are distinct, repeated or nonreal.

lessons.title: Circles, systems of circles and radical axis
lessons.summary: The power of a point with respect to a circle is squared distance from its centre minus squared radius. The radical axis consists of points with equal powers for two circles.

lessons.title: Cayley-Hamilton theorem
lessons.summary: The Cayley–Hamilton theorem states that a square matrix satisfies its own characteristic polynomial. Substitution means matrix powers and the identity matrix, not entrywise scalar evaluation.

lessons.title: Laplace and Fourier transforms
lessons.summary: Transforms represent functions using different mathematical building blocks. The Laplace transform uses exponentially weighted integrals on t≥0; Fourier analysis uses oscillatory complex exponentials or trigonometric components.

lessons.title: Complex analyticity, Cauchy formula and residues
lessons.summary: A complex function is analytic on a domain when it has a complex derivative around every point of that domain. This is stronger than having separate real-variable derivatives.

lessons.title: Generating functions
lessons.summary: A generating function packages a sequence into coefficients of a power series. Algebra on the series becomes a method for reasoning about recurrences and counting.

lessons.title: Euler theorem for homogeneous functions
lessons.summary: A differentiable function is homogeneous of degree k if f(tx,ty)=tᵏf(x,y) on its allowed scaling domain. Euler’s theorem connects this scaling law with partial derivatives.

lessons.title: Positive definite and semidefinite matrices
lessons.summary: A real symmetric matrix is positive definite when xᵀAx>0 for every nonzero real vector x. Positive semidefinite allows zero. These conditions describe quadratic-form curvature and covariance feasibility.

lessons.title: Groups and rings
lessons.summary: A group has a closed associative operation, an identity and an inverse for each element. A ring has an abelian additive group and associative multiplication that distributes over addition; identity conventions should be stated.

lessons.title: Nearest-neighbour distance models
lessons.summary: Nearest-neighbour models predict using nearby labelled training samples under a chosen distance measure. The choice of features, scale, k and tie rule changes the prediction.

lessons.title: Decision trees, impurity and random forests
lessons.summary: A decision tree partitions feature space using conditions chosen to improve target purity. A random forest combines many randomized trees to reduce unstable individual predictions.

lessons.title: Naive Bayes classification
lessons.summary: Naive Bayes uses Bayes’ rule with features assumed conditionally independent given the class. Independence is conditional on the label, not necessarily true across the whole dataset.

lessons.title: SVM, margins and kernel trick
lessons.summary: A support vector machine chooses a separating hyperplane with a large margin, with a soft-margin penalty when strict separation is unsuitable. Support vectors determine the boundary.

lessons.title: K-means and fuzzy clustering
lessons.summary: K-means minimizes within-cluster squared distances by alternating nearest-centroid assignments and mean updates. Fuzzy clustering replaces hard assignments with graded memberships.

lessons.title: Expectation-maximisation and spectral clustering
lessons.summary: Expectation–maximisation fits latent-variable models by alternating expected latent assignments and parameter updates. Spectral clustering instead uses eigenvectors of a similarity-graph operator.

lessons.title: Perceptron and backpropagation
lessons.summary: A perceptron uses a hard decision and mistake-driven updates. Neural-network backpropagation applies the chain rule to a differentiable loss across layers.

lessons.title: Bias-variance and model evaluation
lessons.summary: Evaluation asks how predictions perform on data outside training. Bias and variance describe systematic approximation error and sensitivity to the training sample, respectively.

lessons.title: PCA, whitening and ZCA
lessons.summary: PCA rotates centred data onto covariance eigenvectors, ordered by variance. Whitening additionally rescales those axes to unit variance; ZCA rotates the whitened representation back toward original coordinates.

lessons.title: Bag-of-words, n-grams and TF-IDF
lessons.summary: Bag-of-words counts tokens without retaining global word order. N-grams count consecutive token sequences. TF-IDF weights terms according to local occurrence and corpus-wide rarity.

lessons.title: SIFT, HOG and image-gradient features
lessons.summary: Image-gradient features describe local changes in intensity. HOG aggregates orientation evidence in spatial cells; SIFT adds a keypoint and scale-space construction before forming local descriptors.

lessons.title: SGD, momentum, Adam and initialisation
lessons.summary: Gradient descent updates parameters opposite a loss gradient. Momentum accumulates directional history; Adam combines first and second gradient moments with bias correction. Initialization influences the early flow of activations and gradients.

lessons.title: Regularisation, dropout and batch normalisation
lessons.summary: Regularization changes training to discourage unwanted complexity or sensitivity. L2 penalizes weight magnitude; dropout randomly removes activations during training; normalization standardizes activations and learns an affine rescaling.

lessons.title: Convolution and pooling mathematics
lessons.summary: A convolutional layer shares a local kernel across an input. Most neural libraries compute cross-correlation, although they name the operation convolution. Pooling aggregates local responses.

lessons.title: RNN, LSTM, GRU and gradient stability
lessons.summary: A recurrent model updates a hidden state over a sequence. Backpropagation through time multiplies derivatives across steps, which can make gradients shrink or grow rapidly. LSTM and GRU introduce gates controlling information flow.

lessons.title: Attention and graph neural networks
lessons.summary: Attention forms a data-dependent weighted combination of values. Graph neural networks exchange messages over specified graph edges and aggregate neighbor information. Attention can supply one such aggregation rule.

lessons.title: N-gram probability, smoothing and backoff
lessons.summary: An n-gram language model approximates a token’s conditional probability using a limited history. Smoothing assigns probability to unseen transitions rather than allowing zero counts to eliminate a sequence.

lessons.title: Hidden Markov and maximum entropy models
lessons.summary: A hidden Markov model has latent states with transition probabilities and observed emissions conditioned on states. Maximum entropy models instead normalize exponentiated feature scores for a conditional distribution.

lessons.title: Probabilistic grammars and dynamic-programming parsing
lessons.summary: A probabilistic context-free grammar assigns probabilities to production rules. A parse tree’s probability is the product of the rules applied in that tree. Dynamic programming shares repeated span computations.

lessons.title: Hilbert spaces and quantum measurement
lessons.summary: Quantum pure states are unit vectors in a complex Hilbert space. Measurement probabilities follow the Born rule: squared magnitudes of projections onto the measurement outcomes.

lessons.title: Qubit, Bloch sphere and unitary gates
lessons.summary: A pure qubit can be parameterized by a polar angle θ and azimuth φ on the Bloch sphere. Unitary gates preserve inner products and state norm.

lessons.title: Tensor products, Bell states and entanglement
lessons.summary: Composite quantum states use tensor products of subsystem spaces. An entangled pure state cannot be written as a product of one state per subsystem. Bell states give simple maximally entangled two-qubit examples.
